mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) in a 2008-2023 sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 5% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: The interaction term between PAYEMS and UNRATE is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% suggests accelerating demand growth that anticipates higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeding 0.3% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below -1% followed by a rebound above 0% indicates a supply-side shock that initially depresses sentiment but is followed by a quick recovery that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below -1% then crosses above 0% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative even after INDPRO rebounds above 0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 0.4% while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains unchanged for two months, it indicates a loss of central bank control over inflation, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL month-over-month > 0.4% and FEDFUNDS unchanged for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of 0% returns (p > 0.05) in a 2018-2023 sample.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months without a corresponding rise in jobless claims (PAYEMS) suggests a strengthening labor market that supports equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 months and PAYEMS remains below 150,000 for the same period
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE and PAYEMS is not predictive of forward returns (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies but proxyable via HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests demand-pull dynamics that drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 10% month-over-month while INDPRO decreases by at least 2% month-over-month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the described dual signal.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent supply-side easing (indicated by a downward trend in RSAFS), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days tend to be positive as firms anticipate higher demand for their products, provided the trend in RSAFS persists for at least two months.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS shows a continuous downward trend for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the 2-month RSAFS decline.
